That's only one point of contention in what's going on with Greece. But what /u/BananaBro is referring to is that nations in Greece's position would traditionally devalue their currency, and ramp up exports. Devaluing your currency is the fancy term for making your nation's money worth less in comparison to other currencies - that makes exports cheaper and imports more expensive. It creates a one-way money funnel into your country, because other nations buy your exports, because they're cheap, and your citizens are forced to buy domestic, because they can't afford imported goods anymore. A lot of foreign money coming in, with very little money going back out. Eventually you get enough wealth back in your borders that you can gradually revaluate your money and start digging out of debt.

That's not an option for Greece, now, though, because the Euro isn't their currency to devalue. You can't tell other countries 'right now Greece's money is worth 0.50 Euro, and in 10 years, it'll be worth 0.80 Euro' - because 1 Euro is worth 1 Euro, no matter what country it comes from.

Besides the other valid answers so far, this is also another reason we can't just have one currency, because the global economy frequently relies on differences in exchange rates.

So I feel I'm being really dumb. Starting to need to use Reports more for work and I'll admit I'm pretty new at them and I feel I'm doing something dumb or skipping a step somewhere.

Currently working on a database to keep track of all of our temp workers here at the plant. Got all the workers on a table and have the date the started (fStartDate) and the date they were either hired in or dismissed (fEndDate). In a separate query I use a calculated field and a DateDiff function to get the total number of days between these two dates. I store that number of days in a field called fTotalDays

This is all well and dandy except when I attempt to use the fTotalDays field in a report to show the average number of days a temp works here. Figured it should be simple and make a calculated field that simply reads =Avg([fTotalDays]) and it always comes up as an error. Any reason why it does this? Am I simply skipping a step or is Access attempting to stop me from doing it a way that is antagonistic to proper database philosophy. Any help would be greatly appreciated.
Help using Calculated Fields in a Report

Heck yeah, a post. So there could be a couple of things going on here. To try and track down the problem I made a simple table, query and form. The table had start dates only. I created a standard query based on the table and created "

fTotalDays: DateDiff("d",[startDate],Date())

I then created a form with a textbox and set the control source to

=Avg([fTotalDays])

and got the same error. This is because the form (or report) does not instinctively know what ftotalDays is. I was able to fix this by setting the recordsource for the form to the query I created with fTotalDays. If you already have the field in the reports record source, then you should try adjusting the control source on the report control to this

=Avg(CInt([fTotalDays]))

While I did not have a problem with this in my example, access will sometimes default query fields to strings and you only notice when you try to manipulate them. DateDiff should correctly set it as numeric, but if you have multiple queries in the process it might change.

Alternatively you could use dAvg. You can find information about different dlookup options here - http://codevba.com/msaccess/dlookup_data_retrieval.htm#.VafuFPlVhBc although in my experience dlookup functions can be a little slow, and a little cumbersome to work with.
